title: Partner listing acceptance workflow & asset map
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc maps the end-to-end acceptance workflow for a partner/cloud marketplace listing (covering AWS, Azure, GCP marketplaces and vendor portals). It combines copy drafts, required asset list, technical integration checkpoints, legal/billing requirements, and the minimal acceptance criteria needed to submit a listing and pass initial marketplace validation. Intention: ship a repeatable checklist and copy bank that solutions engineers and GTM can reuse for new partners or self-serve listings.

Executive summary (one line):
Make it easy for partners to create a compliant, conversion-ready listing by providing a clear asset map, templated copy, and a deterministic validation checklist.

Top-level acceptance steps (high level):
1) Confirm partner product tier/offer type (SaaS, Marketplace AMI/container, private offer).
2) Collect assets and legal/billing metadata.
3) Complete marketplace-specific fields + copy variants (short/long).
4) Run technical smoke tests (login flows, entitlement checks, provisioning redirect).
5) Security/compliance sign-off (data handling, telemetry).
6) Submit to marketplace + track validation.

Listing copy bank (short blurb - 1 sentence):
- "Redwood Inference: production-grade LLM inference for reliable, low-latency deployments across hosted, dedicated, and private environments."

Listing copy bank (long description - ~200 words):
- "Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime to run large language model inference with predictable latency, cost efficiency, and enterprise controls. Deploy via hosted API for fast integration, reserved dedicated capacity for predictable throughput, or private VPC/on-premise installs for regulated workloads. Built-in autoscaling, model versioning, and intelligent batching reduce per-token costs while maintaining SLA-backed reliability. Integrate with single-sign-on, audit logging, and customer-managed keys to meet enterprise security needs. For platform teams, Redwood offers rollout controls (canary/A-B), observability dashboards, and quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets—helping product and ML teams ship LLM features with confidence."

Key benefits bullets (for marketplace UI):
- Consistent low-latency inference across environments
- Predictable unit economics via batching & caching
- SLA-backed Dedicated options + Private deployments for compliance
- Observability and rollout tooling for safe releases
- Integrations: SSO, KMS, audit logs, VPC peering

Call-to-action variants (for A/B tests):
- "Start a free trial (5k tokens)"
- "Request a Dedicated capacity demo"
- "Deploy a private evaluation in your VPC"

Mandatory assets checklist (visual / marketing):
- Company logo (svg + png 1024x1024)
- Product screenshots (3) with captions and alt text (plain UI + telemetry dashboard + rollout dashboard)
- 60–120s explainer video (mp4) and short transcript
- One-pager PDF: pricing summary, contact, trial terms
- Supported deployment diagram (SVG, labeled)

Technical & integration checklist (dev/SE items):
- Tenant onboarding flow documented (SaaS) with redirect URIs and example tokens
- Entitlement API endpoints (doc + example responses)
- SSO integration guidance (SAML/OIDC) and metadata file
- Marketplace-specific deployment artifact (AMI, container image, or SaaS redirect URL)
- Health-check endpoints for marketplace validation (readme with curl examples)
- Public telemetry/metrics endpoints and sample dashboards for Marketplace QA

Billing & legal checklist:
- Contract terms for private/enterprise (template attached)
- Pricing tier matrix (hosted per-token, dedicated reserved nodes, private license fees)
- Trial terms and metering rules (trial limits, grace periods)
- Tax & invoicing info for partner account (billing contact + tax id)
- Marketplace-specific commercial setup (private offers, revenue share rates)

Security & compliance sign-offs:
- Data handling statement for marketplace (what is persisted, retention windows)
- KMS/HSM integration notes for Private deployments
- Penetration test summary or attestation (if required by marketplace)
- SOC2 / ISO references and links to artefacts

Validation tests (minimal acceptance criteria):
- Listing copy complete (short + long + three bullet benefits)
- Screenshots present & validated (no PII in images)
- Trial provisioning works end-to-end in a staging marketplace account
- Entitlement APIs return correct grant states in 5s under test load
- SSO flow completes and maps to a partner tenant role
- Billing mapping tested: metered events appear in test billing artifacts

Operational runbook notes (post-listing):
- Monitor first-72-hour onboarding metrics: trial starts, failed provisionings, support tickets
- Assign on-call owner for marketplace escalations (SE + CS)
- Run a conversion review after 14 days (trial->paid metrics)

Owner & roles (recommended):
- Listing lead: Solutions Engineering (owner: Ethan Rivera)
- Copy + assets: GTM Content (owner: Maya Thompson)
- Technical QA: Platform Eng (owner: Noah Li)
- Legal review: Finance & Legal (contact: Priya Kapoor)

Timeline (example, 6–8 business days to submit):
- Day 0–1: Asset collection and copy sync
- Day 2–3: Technical integration + smoke tests in staging
- Day 4: Security & billing sign-off
- Day 5–6: Final QA and marketplace submission
- Day 7–14: Marketplace validation & feedback loop

Common failure modes & remediation tips:
- Missing alt-text on screenshots -> block for accessibility; provide captions
- SSO metadata mismatch -> re-generate metadata with correct ACS/Entity IDs and re-test
- Trial provisioning timeouts -> add async hook for longer activation windows and surface progress to end-user
- Billing metering not firing -> instrument server-side events and validate with test invoices

Metrics to track after publish:
- Time to first successful trial provisioning (median)"
notes: This is a working draft intended to be used as the single-source checklist for partner listings. Iterate copy based on marketplace UI limits (character counts) and add marketplace-specific fields (e.g., AWS AMI IDs, Azure Offer IDs) before submission. Also link the final assets folder once ready: drive:/shared_drives/go-to-market/assets/partner-listings/<partner-name>
